listenings.text: Hi Andreia, this is Ken Walsh. I'm chairing your session on Thursday, and I just wanted to go over a few details. Your talk is at ten forty, in Room B. You have ten minutes for the talk and five minutes for questions, so please don't go over. Could you send me your slide deck by Wednesday at noon? I'd like to load everything on one computer before the session starts. Please remember that your first slide has to be the disclosure slide, even if you have nothing to disclose. You'll speak from the podium, and there is a pointer and a small clock in front of you. At eight minutes, I'll give you a signal, so you know you have two minutes left. I read your abstract, and I think the audience will love it. See you on Thursday.

Good morning, everyone, and thank you, Ken, for the introduction. Let me start with a question. How long does it take your team to prepare a robotic room? Three years ago, when we started our robotic program at Einstein Hospital, it took us more than forty minutes, and we had never worked with a robot before. Today, I'd like to share what our nursing team learned in our first two hundred cases. I'll start by telling you how we built the team. Then I'll move on to our findings, and finally, I'll talk about the limitations of our study. Before I start, I have nothing to disclose. So, let's begin.
